text.p: Following are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The cabinet suspended all Zakat and Ushr (Islamic taxes) collection committees and handed the job to deputy commissioners.
- The government has stopped all major banks and financial institutions from rescheduling unpaid loans before elections on February 3.
- At least 10 people have died in the last two days because of a cold wave sweeping through the southern province of Sindh.
- The Sindh provincial government has set up a committee to review charges against detained leaders of the Mohajir National Movement (MQM) and other party activists.
- The government faces an alarming situation after an influx of 75,000 Afghan refugees into Pakistan in the last few months.
- Japan has allowed its two major trading houses to launch $400 million of yen-denominated samurai bonds on behalf of the government of Pakistan early next year, sources said.
- The rupee has gained 2.5 percent against the dollar in the kerb market in the last month amid oversupply of the dollar and low demand.
- The cabinet cut the number of import items required to be valued by a pre-shipment inspection agency and decided ultimately to terminate the contract of one of the two firms.
- The Privatisation Commission is likely to hold fresh bidding for the sale of state-run Pak-Saudi Fertilizer Ltd.
- Palm oil imports declined 25 percent in November compared to October because of economic and political uncertainty.
- The Privatisation Commission is likely to be reconstituted within a week to accelerate the privatisation process in a more transparent and smooth manner.
- Defence Minister Shahid Hamid told the Senate (upper house) that state-run Pakistan International Airlines will increase its fares from 10 to 15 percent from December 16.
- The cabinet has cancelled a 3.0-billion rupee contract with IBM for computerisation of national identity cards.
